svg.title: Tsallis q-Gaussians and conformal flatness of the q-escort
svg.desc: Left: logarithm of the q-Gaussian density for q = 0.5 (compact support), q = 1 (Gaussian, a parabola on this scale) and q = 1.5 (power-law tail). Right: relative spread of the eigenvalues of the ratio of the escort metric to the Fisher metric at 25 random points of the simplex: about 1e-6 (noise) for a power function chi, up to 0.2 for the kappa-exponential.
svg.text: Is the q-metric conformal to Fisher?
Left: expqof a quadratic has finite support for q < 1 and a power-law tail for q > 1.
Right: eigenvalues of gF⁻¹ Hess ψχ(escort metric against Fisher): equal for a power χ (the 10⁻⁶ spread is
finite-difference noise), unequal for the κ-exponential: only the q-escort geometry is conformal (Theorem 4.14).
